text: Last lesson you registered a model version. Now you put it behind a real-time endpoint: one request in, one prediction out, in milliseconds. This is what a support screen or a checkout page calls.

A deployment needs four things. The model, as a registered name and version. A scoring script with an init and a run function. An environment, which is a Docker image plus conda packages. And compute: an instance type and an instance count.

The endpoint is the stable name and U R L, with an authentication mode. Behind it sit deployments. In this Microsoft diagram, ninety percent of traffic goes to a blue deployment running model version one, and ten percent to a green one running version two. That is how you roll out a new model safely.

The scoring script is plain Python. Init runs once when the container starts, so load the model there. Run is called for every request and receives the request body as a string. Parse the JSON, build a data frame, score it, and return something JSON friendly.

Test before you deploy. The docs describe an inference server package that runs your script locally, without Docker. I ran this exact script in it. A good request returned risks of point nine one seven and point zero three seven. A bad request returned a five hundred error, and the real cause, a missing key, appeared only in the server log. Always read the logs.

In the S D K, you define a managed online endpoint with a name and an authentication mode. Then a deployment with the model, environment, scoring script, instance type and count. Then you route all traffic to blue. This is illustrative, since we have no Azure account, and creation can take many minutes.

The studio shows live traffic, the scoring script, the instance size and count, and a Test tab. To ship a new model, add a green deployment with no traffic, mirror ten percent to it, then shift ten percent live, then all of it. And an endpoint keeps compute running, so delete it when you finish.
Next: batch endpoints, for when nobody is waiting on a single answer.
